title: Coherent modules on a locally Noetherian space are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $Z$ be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Work in the abelian category of module sheaves on $(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Locally Noetherian means that etale scheme charts are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Coherent means that on every affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], the module sheaf is associated to a finitely generated $R$-module $N$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with value $B\otimes_RN$ on affine etale maps $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. The zero module is coherent. For every morphism $u:F\to G$ of coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, its kernel and cokernel in this module-sheaf category are coherent. For every short exact sequence $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ in this category with $F,G$ coherent, $E$ is coherent. Coherence is invariant under isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 07UC (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian), with coherence characterized by Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian).

proof.text: Fix any affine etale chart $v:V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$ with $R$ Noetherian. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], its module pullback is restriction to the localized site, hence is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Write $A_V$ for the fully faithful scheme Zariski/etale comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]; it is exact into the ambient etale module category by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], $A_V(\widetilde N)$ has value $B\otimes_RN$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$. Consequently a coherent space module restricts to $A_V(\widetilde N)$ for finite $N$. These restrictions are site quasi-coherent, and the local-presentation condition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] then makes the module quasi-coherent on $Z$: each object $T$ of $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a locally Noetherian scheme, so by [pqf-def-locnoeth] it has an affine open cover by spectra $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of Noetherian rings; each $\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to T\to Z$ is such a chart, and we take the local presentations of $A_{\operatorname{Spec}R_i}(\widetilde{N_i})$ there. The affine finite-type criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] and [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] show that $\widetilde N$ is coherent on $V$, which is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] since $R$ is Noetherian. Conversely a coherent Zariski module $H$ on $V$ is quasi-coherent of finite type by the latter criterion; the affine criterion makes $N=H(V)$ finite, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) gives $H\simeq\widetilde N$. Thus $A_V(H)$ has exactly the finite-module formula required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), affine chart characterization; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03LV/03LW; descent.tex Tags 03DX and 06VE(5); coherent.tex Tag 01XZ; properties.tex Tag 01PB; schemes.tex Tags 01HV, 01I9 and 01IA.

proof.text: For $u:F\to G$ coherent, on the chart $V$ of step 1 write $F|_V\simeq A_V(H_F)$ and $G|_V\simeq A_V(H_G)$ with $H_F,H_G$ coherent. Full faithfulness of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] lifts $u|_V$ to a Zariski module map $h:H_F\to H_G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum](1), its scheme kernel $K$ and cokernel $C$ are coherent, and so is the image of $h$, the cokernel of $K\to H_F$; all three are quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Exactness of $A_V$ in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] applied to $0\to K\to H_F\to\operatorname{Im}h\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{Im}h\to H_G\to C\to0$ identifies $A_V(K)$ and $A_V(C)$ with the ambient etale kernel and cokernel of $u|_V$. Exact restriction from step 1 identifies these with $(\ker u)|_V$ and $(\operatorname{coker}u)|_V$. The converse comparison of step 1 gives the required finite-module formulas for these two restrictions. Since $V$ was an arbitrary Noetherian affine etale chart, this proves both global coherence assertions.

source.place: Tag 07UC (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian), reduction to schemes; modules.tex Tag 01BY(2),(3), coherent.tex Tag 01XZ, descent.tex Tags 03DX and 06VE(5).

proof.text: For $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ with coherent endpoints, step 1 makes $F,G$ quasi-coherent on $Z$. Thus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-extension-closed] makes $E$ quasi-coherent, without any prior assumption on $E$. Exact restriction to $V$ gives a short exact sequence of etale modules. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] writes its terms and maps as the $A_V$-images of a complex $H_F\to H_E\to H_G$ of quasi-coherent Zariski modules. This complex is short exact: its kernels, images, cokernels and homology are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]; the exact functor $A_V$ of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] sends its three homology objects to zero. Full faithfulness reflects zero objects (the identity of an object mapping to zero must be zero), so all three homology objects vanish. Step 1 says $H_F,H_G$ are coherent. The extension clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] now gives coherence of $H_E$. The converse comparison of step 1 gives the finite-module formula for $E|_V$. This holds on every chart $V$, proving coherence of $E$.

source.place: Tag 07UC, extension case in the scheme reduction; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1(4); descent.tex Tags 03DX and 06VE(5); schemes.tex Tags 01IC and 01LB; modules.tex Tag 01BY(4).

proof.text: The zero module on every affine chart is $B\mapsto B\otimes_R0=0$, and the zero $R$-module is generated by the empty set. Hence the zero module is coherent. If $F\simeq F'$ and $F$ is coherent, restrict the isomorphism to a chart and compose its inverse with $F|_V\simeq(B\mapsto B\otimes_RN)$. This gives the same finite-module formula for $F'|_V$ with the same finitely generated $N$. The inverse isomorphism gives the converse, so coherence is invariant under isomorphism.
